summary: First functional medicinal-material/formula/interaction graph: one new taxon Piper longum, eight distinct preparation materials including clove essential oil vs flower bud, authenticated Trikatu ingredient components, and separately sourced human piperine-curcumin exposure interaction. No medical dose, formula efficacy, or assumed synergy.

organisms.geographic_context: Eastern Himalaya, South Asia and parts of Southeast Asia; used in Ayurvedic Trikatu formulas.
organisms.part_and_preparation_note: Dried fruit/infructescence in medicinal contexts. Not equivalent to black pepper Piper nigrum or Piper retrofractum under ambiguous common names.

medicinal_materials.preparation: dried ginger rhizome used in named Trikatu composition
medicinal_materials.processing: drying and powdering discussed in traditional formula category; ratios not verified
medicinal_materials.limitations: Trikatu's ginger component is distinct from fresh ginger, volatile oil or purified gingerol; named constituent is not safe-dosing evidence.

medicinal_materials.processing: drying, often powdered in studied Trikatu descriptions
medicinal_materials.limitations: This ingredient is Piper nigrum, not Piper longum, and whole fruit is not a purified piperine formulation.

medicinal_materials.preparation: Piper longum long pepper fruit used in Trikatu
medicinal_materials.processing: dried fruit/infructescence, processing and ratio not independently established in source
medicinal_materials.limitations: Taxon must be authenticated as Piper longum L.; Piper retrofractum and other long-pepper species should not be silently substituted.

medicinal_materials.preparation: Caryophylli Flos / Ding Xiang dried flower-bud medicinal material
medicinal_materials.limitations: Only dried bud identity and historic monograph context; not a concentrated essential oil or guaranteed safe ingestion.

medicinal_materials.processing: volatile-oil extraction, not equivalent to culinary buds
medicinal_materials.tradition: commercial topical / aromatic applications and laboratory studies
medicinal_materials.limitations: Concentrated clove oil can cause chemical burns and severe toxicity when swallowed; this record is not a product-use instruction.

medicinal_materials.processing: leaf drying / herbal preparation as discussed in EU monograph
medicinal_materials.limitations: Peppermint leaf preparation is not the same as peppermint essential oil capsules or undiluted oil.

medicinal_materials.preparation: Menthae piperitae aetheroleum / peppermint essential oil
medicinal_materials.processing: steam-distilled volatile-oil material; standardized commercial products differ
medicinal_materials.limitations: Oil formulation, enteric coating and intended route matter; undiluted essential oil must not be treated as mint tea.

medicinal_materials.preparation: fu ling / hoelen dried fungal sclerotium
medicinal_materials.processing: traditionally dried sclerotium; exact processing/species requires authentication
medicinal_materials.limitations: Older literature under Poria/Wolfiporia cocos may mix taxa; no chemical equivalence to other mushrooms is established.

formulas.name: Trikatu
formulas.claimed_use: Historically combined three pungent spices in Ayurvedic multi-herb practice; reviewed for hypothetical digestive, immunomodulatory or bioavailability-related properties.
formulas.limitations: Named composition is documented; no clinical claim that Trikatu cures COVID-19, infections, or any disease. Formula descriptions and ingredient ratios can vary by textual lineage. Piperine can change exposure to other drugs; contraindications and safe dosing cannot be inferred from the historical name.

formula_components.limitations: No therapeutic dosage, fraction or formula processing duration confirmed by this record.
Piper nigrum and purified piperine are distinct exposures. No safe combination dose established.
Actual authenticated botanical species and product purity matter; no ratio or dose is inferred.

interaction_evidence.method: Controlled short-window serum concentration comparison in healthy volunteers; animal experiments also included.
interaction_evidence.observation: Piperine coadministration increased measured systemic curcumin exposure in the specific experimental setting. This was a pharmacokinetic endpoint, NOT evidence of enhanced medical treatment effectiveness.
interaction_evidence.limitations: Study used isolated compounds in a specific short-duration, high-exposure experiment; cannot generalize to culinary turmeric+pepper, Trikatu, other medications or long-term safety. Piperine may alter drug handling, so interactions matter.
interaction_evidence.assay_endpoint: human serum concentration and bioavailability of curcumin

cultural_uses.preparation: a named component of multi-herb Trikatu; not a preparation instruction
cultural_uses.reported_use: Traditional formula pairs long pepper with ginger and black pepper in Trikatu; other attributed effects are not necessarily supported by clinical trials.
cultural_uses.limitations: Species authentication, dose, processing, and product interactions require separate evidence.

practice_claims.tradition: South Asian classical Ayurvedic compound formulas
framework: Trikatu multi-herb mixture; no unverified rasa/virya/dosha labels assigned
practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Historically used as a component of Trikatu for a variety of claimed health conditions and to modify other medicines' activity.
practice_claims.preparation: dried long-pepper material used with black pepper and ginger; see FORM-TRIKATU
practice_claims.route: oral historical preparations; not a recommended route or regimen
practice_claims.limitations: No source-backed dose, safety or medical efficacy for long pepper alone from this paper; do not automatically generalize Trikatu results to purified piperine.

domain_notes.text: Piperine-containing pepper products may affect xenobiotic pharmacokinetics; this does not prove improved metabolism or energy in people.
Traditional digestive and other uses in Trikatu are documented historically, not established treatments in controlled human efficacy studies.
No source-verified specific cognitive therapeutic result for Piper longum has been entered in this batch.
No reliable evidence of an isolated long-pepper anxiolytic or antidepressant effect has been indexed in this batch.

safety.alert: Medicinal long pepper is not interchangeable with black pepper or other Piper species. Piperine-associated pharmacokinetic changes may alter medicine exposure; safe dose and use in pregnancy, children and chronic illnesses have not been established by the Trikatu composition reviews.
